# `sim/particles/ParticleSchema.js`

> **Source:** `engine/sim/particles/ParticleSchema.js`

ParticleSchema.js - Unified JSON Schema for Particle System Defines consistent data structures for: - Particle buffer layouts (GPU data) - Shader uniform parameters - Emitter configurations - Snapshot formats for rewind All particle-related code should use these schemas for consistency.

## Functions

### `packParticleMeta(size, renderMode, shape, behavior = 0, mass = 1.0, drag = 0.02)`

Pack meta.w value from individual components (full format with physics) Format: mass * 1e8 + drag * 1e6 + size * 1e4 + renderMode * 1e3 + shape * 10 + behavior

**Parameters:**

- `size` *(number)* — Particle size (0-99)
- `renderMode` *(number)* — Render mode ID (0-9)
- `shape` *(number)* — Shape ID (0-9)
- `behavior` *(number)* — Behavior ID (0-9)
- `mass` *(number)* — Particle mass (0.0-9.9, encoded as 0-99)
- `drag` *(number)* — Air resistance (0.0-0.99, encoded as 0-99)

### `unpackParticleMeta(packed)`

Unpack meta.w value to individual components

### `getBehaviorId(behaviorName)`

Get behavior ID from behavior name

### `validateField(value, fieldSchema)`

Validate a value against a schema field

### `validateEmitterConfig(config)`

Validate an emitter config against schema

### `createDefaultEmitterConfig(overrides = {})`

Create a default emitter config

### `createDefaultParticleParams(overrides = {})`

Create a default particle params uniform buffer data

### `createEmptySnapshot(time, frameIndex)`

Create an empty particle snapshot

### `createEmitterSnapshot(emitter)`

Create an emitter snapshot from live emitter state

### `getShapeId(shapeName)`

Get shape ID from shape name

### `getRenderModeId(modeName)`

Get render mode ID from mode name

### `getShapeName(shapeId)`

Get shape name from ID

### `getRenderModeName(modeId)`

Get render mode name from ID

### `serializeEmitterConfig(config)`

Serialize emitter config to JSON-safe object

### `deserializeEmitterConfig(json)`

Deserialize emitter config from JSON

### `serializeSnapshot(snapshot)`

Serialize particle snapshot to JSON-safe object

### `deserializeSnapshot(json)`

Deserialize particle snapshot from JSON

## Constants

- `PARTICLE_BUFFER_SCHEMA` — Per-particle data layout in GPU buffers. Each particle uses 3 vec4s (48 bytes total).
- `FRAME_UNIFORMS_SCHEMA` — Frame uniforms passed to all particle shaders
- `PARTICLE_PARAMS_SCHEMA` — Per-draw particle parameters
- `FORCE_PARAMS_SCHEMA` — Force parameters uniform (group 2 binding 0 in main particle compute shader) Controls global wind, turbulence, force points, vortex, and velocity clamping.
- `PARTICLE_SHAPES` — Shape types for particle rendering
- `RENDER_MODES` — Render modes for particle blending
- `PARTICLE_BEHAVIORS` — Behavior types for particle movement patterns
- `EMITTER_CONFIG_SCHEMA` — Complete emitter configuration schema
- `ELEMENT_LAYER_SCHEMA` — Element layer for emitter mixing
- `PARTICLE_SNAPSHOT_ENTRY_SCHEMA` — Single particle snapshot entry
- `EMITTER_SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA` — Emitter state snapshot
- `PARTICLE_SYSTEM_SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA` — Complete particle system snapshot

## Notes & Examples

### Physics Engine Integration

The physics system provides rigid body dynamics, collision detection, and raycasting. Bodies have shapes (box, sphere, mesh), mass properties, and constraints. The GPU physics engine accelerates broad-phase collision detection and particle systems.

**Example: Creating physics bodies**
```js
import { PhysicsWorld } from 'engine/physics/PhysicsWorld.js';
import { RigidBody } from 'engine/physics/RigidBody.js';
import { BoxShape, SphereShape } from 'engine/physics/Shapes.js';

const world = new PhysicsWorld({ gravity: [0, -9.8, 0] });

// Static ground
const ground = new RigidBody({
  type: 'static',
  shape: new BoxShape(10, 1, 10),
  position: [0, -0.5, 0]
});
world.addBody(ground);

// Dynamic box
const box = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  mass: 1,
  shape: new BoxShape(1, 1, 1),
  position: [0, 5, 0],
  restitution: 0.5  // Bounciness
});
world.addBody(box);
```

**Advanced: Collision detection and raycasting**
```js
// Raycast to find what the player is looking at
const hit = world.raycast(camera.position, camera.forward, 100);
if (hit) {
  console.log('Hit entity:', hit.body.entityId);
  console.log('Hit point:', hit.point);
  console.log('Hit normal:', hit.normal);
  
  // Apply impulse at hit point
  hit.body.applyImpulse([0, 10, 0], hit.point);
}

// Shapecast (swept sphere) for character movement
const sweep = world.shapecast(
  player.position,           // Start
  desiredPosition,           // End
  new SphereShape(0.5),    // Player capsule radius
  { ignore: player.body }  // Don't collide with self
);
if (sweep.hit) {
  // Slide along wall
  player.position = sweep.position;
}
```

**Advanced: Constraints and joints**
```js
import { HingeConstraint, FixedConstraint } from 'engine/physics/Constraints.js';

// Door hinge
const doorHinge = new HingeConstraint({
  bodyA: doorFrame,
  bodyB: door,
  pivot: [0, 1, 0],      // Hinge location
  axis: [0, 1, 0],       // Hinge axis (Y up)
  limits: [-90, 90]      // Open angle range in degrees
});
world.addConstraint(doorHinge);

// Ragdoll joint (ball-and-socket)
const shoulder = new FixedConstraint({
  bodyA: torso,
  bodyB: arm,
  pivotA: [0.5, 1.5, 0],  // Shoulder position on torso
  pivotB: [0, 0, 0]       // Shoulder position on arm
});
world.addConstraint(shoulder);
```

**Advanced: Continuous collision detection (CCD)**
```js
// Fast-moving objects need CCD to not tunnel through walls
const projectile = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  shape: new SphereShape(0.1),
  mass: 0.1,
  ccd: { enabled: true, sweptSphereRadius: 0.1 },
  linearDamping: 0  // No air resistance for bullets
});
projectile.velocity = [0, 0, 100];  // Very fast
world.addBody(projectile);
```

**Gotchas:**
- **Units**: Physics uses meters, kilograms, seconds. A 1-unit cube is 1 meter.
- **Time step**: Fixed time step (1/60) gives stable simulation; variable dt causes explosions.
- **Collision layers**: Use collision masks to filter what collides (player vs enemy, bullet vs world).
- **Sleeping**: At-rest bodies sleep to save CPU — wake them before applying forces.
